Action 1 — Cream banner test, new campaign (launch 11-17). |DETAILS|
  • Domain: creative (format) and campaign.
  • Entity: new campaign "Jaiwasi | Cream Banner Test | W exc. J&K Assam Bihar | 17/11/26". Product: Cream Cotton Dress (AetEOIP_91ZR).
  • Change: Create a new CBO campaign (budget set at campaign level), lowest cost, ₹500/day.
    • One ad set with the same audience as ad set 120252913189670163 "Bestsellers' Videos": women only, Assam, J&K and Bihar excluded, same age range, open audience.
    • One ad: a static banner built from the Cream product images (get_product_images for AetEOIP_91ZR). Use the copy and headline of the Cream video ad (120252913311140163, video id 1986922825279078).
    • Only the format changes (video to banner).
    • Start only after the seller confirms size stock for Cream SKU 5M95SCz- (set out of stock on 11-11 [get_ts_shopdeck_changelogs]). Without that confirmation, this action does not run.

  • Why: this is the format test of the creative winner. The Cream video has 8.04% S/GMV on 90 orders [last 7 days · get_ad_level_data] and 9.90% on 420 Meta purchases [8 weeks · get_ad_level_data]. Cream earns after RTO:

    • RTO is 34% against a break-even RTO of 55%.
    • Profit is ₹4,812 a week.
    • Ad cost is ₹78 per shipped order [7d · get_unit_economics].
    • Break-even CPP is ₹154 with GST. Divided by 1.18, it is ₹130.51 ex-GST.
    • Stock is 565 units, 63.8 days of cover [get_inventory_check].

    The ad mapping shows only video rows for Cream. Some mapping rows have blank product ids, so a hidden banner is not fully ruled out. The test moves CPP (cost per purchase) and C2PR (purchases ÷ link clicks) through the format. It sits in its own campaign, so the earning Bestsellers Videos campaign is not edited.

    Overlap risk. The banner runs on the same audience as the Cream video, which took ₹24,487.49 of that campaign's ₹27,968.93 8-week spend (87.55% = 24,487.49 ÷ 27,968.93) [8 weeks · get_ad_level_data]. Some banner orders may be orders the video would have got anyway. No tool measures this share. I assume 25% (an unmeasured stress case). The bridge uses it. At zero overlap the effect is −₹512.10 / +₹597.78 / +₹1,707.65 (fail / mid / pass). The overlap share at which the mid effect falls to zero is 17.86%. For the pass case it is 32.79%. With the 25% overlap, the pass gain of ₹405.74 is under the ₹500 size rule, and the mid effect is negative. I keep the test for three reasons: - The 25% is an assumption, not a measurement. - The gate below measures the real overlap before more than ₹2,000 is spent. - Cream is the one product that earns after RTO, and a format that wins lowers the dependence on one video.

    Cream is already 19.39% of W46 orders, so the test also adds to that dependence. - Effect: per week, at ₹500/day, with 25% overlap. The orders are net of overlap. - Fail (stops at the ₹2,000 gate, cost per order 2 × ₹68.04 = ₹136.08): −₹884.07, 11.02 orders. - Mid: −₹239.17, 24.80 orders. - Pass (cost per order ₹68.04, the Banners Open W46 banner comparable): +₹405.74, 38.58 orders. - Row S/GMV is 30.94% / 18.90% / 15.47%. - Checkpoint: judge at ₹2,000 lifetime spend (about 11-21). - Pass needs both: - 20 or more banner orders, which is S/GMV 17.05% or lower, under the 17.26% console BE0 (2,000 ÷ (20 × 586.54)). - Cream video orders over the test days no more than 15% under their pre-launch pace. The pace is 12.86 a day (90 orders ÷ 7 days, [11-09 to 11-15 · get_ad_level_data]). 15% sits under the 17.86% mid break-even overlap. - Then raise ₹500 → ₹600 on one step, then continue at +20% every 48 hours. - Fail is 19 or fewer banner orders, or video orders more than 15% down. Launch one Open Audience video campaign at Rs 1,000/day on 5 perfume SKUs. |DETAILS| Instruction: Create one Open Audience campaign on ad account 1061446613564558 at Rs.1,000/day with five video ads - R Oudh Rose Saffron Bergamot Oud Perfume (Rs.599), Marj Oud Saffron Cashmere Wood Perfume (Rs.599), Rh Bergamot Apple Cinnamon EDP (Rs.599), Silk Saffron Vanilla Floral Woody Perfume (Rs.499) and Caramel Oud Vanilla Rose Perfume (Rs.449). Age 18-65, all genders, India-wide excluding Assam, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka, Punjab, West Bengal and Bihar. No ROAS floor - let it bid uncapped. It goes live as it is built. Reasoning: This account has never recorded marketing spend, so there is no performance history to diagnose and the launch rests on catalogue and category priors. Lookalike is ruled out on the seller's own data - 0 delivered orders and no pixel purchase signal means no seed exists - so Open Audience is the correct first stage. The targeting shape (age 18-65, all genders, Advantage+, India-wide minus six serviceability states) is carried from the strongest comparable ad set on record via get_adset_details_for_product_id: ad set 120230954155040178 on product 7jIaZ4ty shows Rs 16,821 spend on the product, 456 ad-set orders and ad-set S/GMV 23.85%, with excluded_geo_locations naming Assam, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka, Punjab region, West Bengal and Bihar. A second comparable (s6rupeXi, 666 lifetime orders) independently ran age 18-65 with all genders, so two sellers agreeing makes this a prior rather than an anecdote. All six geo keys were re-resolved through search_meta_geo_locations this run and match the carried set exactly: Assam 1725, Jammu and Kashmir 1732, Karnataka 1738, Punjab 1742, West Bengal 1746, Bihar 1752. The five products were picked for scent-family spread so the first week discriminates between families rather than between SKUs of one family, and each carries CAC headroom to fund paid traffic: recomputed from get_seller_category_level_benchmarking figures (bm_logs_cost 87.28 per AWB) at 12%/15% commission, max affordable CAC is Rs 149.84 / Rs 131.87 on the Rs 599 tier, Rs 107.84 / Rs 94.37 on Rs 449 and Rs 91.84 / Rs 76.87 on Rs 499. No roas_floor is set, so the campaign runs LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP and buys the first week of learning - the account has no ratio of its own for Meta to bid against, and a floor above anything it has achieved would starve delivery. The ad account id 1061446613564558 comes from get_seller_config_build, the only source for a never-spent seller, and get_meta_campaign_settings confirms no campaign exists for this seller, so this is genuinely the first one and nothing needs funding. All five products confirmed active, visible and in stock at 20 units each with cost prices recorded (get_inventory_check, get_product_details_by_product_id). Five separate video renders were started this run, one per product, and each returned its own handle: job_apHfkg6vtu93, job_r60wGBnGlZWg, job_NSB2R96aotpl, job_zwx2Tk6sb0EV, job_QZ3mXSINOwd5. The campaign is held until all five land; a render that dies costs its product the ad, not the campaign., Ask seller to cut rupee cost of goods on the launch SKUs and settle the premium-SKU and coupon questions. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller to get fresh supplier cost quotes for the launch perfumes and bring the rupee cost down - from Rs.290 toward Rs.225 on the Rs.599 bottles and from Rs.260 toward Rs.205 on Silk Saffron Vanilla (1G72XyDx), a 10-20% improvement on cost, not on the COGS percentage. Show them that their own Caramel Oud Vanilla Rose (4Nuyno2j) is sourced at Rs.200 for the same kind of bottle. Also ask on the same call: can we add a Rs.699-Rs.799 premium perfume, what coupon bands do they want once we have our own order data, and what to do with Qhawa Cinnamon Cardamom (QhzkppSY) at Rs.649 and Rs.315 cost, which is priced above the market ceiling. Reasoning: fetch_hygiene_actions returns "Update all visible SKUs to have cogs less than 50%" covering all 51 SKUs with seller_consent: false, and the launch set's COGS of 44.5-52.1% sits 12-19pp above the fragrances category benchmark of 32.93% (get_seller_category_level_benchmarking). This is the only lever that fixes the hygiene flag and the margin squeeze at the same time, and it is not a price move - COGS% is cost divided by price, so cutting price raises COGS% while shrinking the CAC headroom. I recomputed the headroom from the same inputs: at 12% commission the Rs 599 tier supports max CAC Rs 149.84 at COGS 48.4%, and closing half the gap to the 32.93% category benchmark lifts that to roughly Rs 212 - about 40% more traffic fundable at the same margin. The seller's own catalogue proves a lower cost is achievable: qdst7AVLwd3T is sourced at Rs 200 for the same fragrance bottle type that uSA5hWAsKnkz costs Rs 260 to source (both confirmed live via get_product_details_by_product_id). The decision rule: if the seller cannot move cost within four weeks, the Rs 449 and Rs 499 SKUs (max CAC Rs 69-92) become hard to fund with paid traffic and the account should shift up to the Rs 599/649 tier or to a marketplace-first plan. On Qhawa Cinnamon Cardamom (PHp8Skqixjsi, confirmed live at Rs 649 with Rs 315 cost and 48.5% COGS): a cut to Rs 599 lifts COGS to 52.6% and cuts max CAC from Rs 168.84 to Rs 124.84 at 12% commission, so a price cut is not the answer - either its cost falls or its price falls, and it stays out of the launch set until one of those happens. Note the COGS coupling trap - no COGS action is recommended against a rupee-denominated external reference, because get_internal_pricing_similarity returned no matches, so the ask must come from the seller's own supplier quotes and not be inferred from a percentage we moved ourselves. On the coupon ladder, active_generic_coupon_count is 0 and aov_for_coupon_check is null (no order history), so the correct 2x/3x bands cannot be computed yet and are not set blind. On the premium SKU, search_similar_products showed every product with over 300 lifetime orders in this category sits between Rs 499 and Rs 799 while this catalogue tops out at Rs 649, and a Rs 699-Rs.799 SKU would carry roughly Rs 210-Rs 230 of ad-cost headroom versus Rs 150 at Rs 599. Raising it before or alongside launch day is what decides whether week 2 is a scale-up or a stockout, because a stockout on a pre-live account reads as a failed product rather than an empty shelf., Ask seller to bring the printed cotton tee cost from Rs 378 to Rs 360 per unit. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller to bring the cost price of the printed cotton tees from Rs 378 to Rs 360 per unit across the whole printed-tee catalogue (ssb-001, ssb-002, ssb-003, ssb-004, ssb-005, ssb-006, AiddSRbv, bQDfeXsD, CwWyg9gc, CdePCNI9, hnHMtY6u, HxVMK1Uu, I2FNJFZr, IKEciJoY, IoyyHwVS, Iz6MqN7d, Jckc5up1, Jq3lkIJe, P_8B2MVM, QqIPE2ce, sW8fntvZ, tXJkZQqp, u60AcgOH, Ud9qWjbW, CWeVlnyG, 2RC_y0YL, VmsTYGDS, YXyfw6oh, ilTKTc8T, o15SYWqy, qw5MLBNE, usiT9cnD), holding the selling price at Rs 749. Reasoning: fetch_hygiene_actions returned "Update all visible SKUs to have cogs less than 50%", and get_seller_catalogue confirms cost Rs 378 against price Rs 749 across all 36 live products, i.e. COGS 50.47% - only 0.47pp over the standard, or Rs 3.5 per unit. A cost of Rs 360 puts COGS at 48.06% and clears it outright. Critically, this ask has a rupee-denominated reference: the seller's own cost of Rs 378 is the rupee figure and the Rs 360 target is derived from it, so no percentage was moved by our own arithmetic to manufacture the ask. A 4.8% improvement is well inside a plausible 10-20% sourcing conversation. No price change is proposed alongside this, and none should be: recomputing maximum survivable S/GMV on the category's own inputs (unisex-clothing bm_rto 39.10%, bm_logs_cost Rs 88.96/order, bm_cogs 45.35%, commission 8%) gives 22.0% at Rs 749, 17.0% at Rs 699 and 11.2% at Rs 649, so a cut moves the account toward loss rather than toward profit, and it raises COGS further (Rs 699 = 54.08%, Rs 649 = 58.24%). Do not recommend a COGS increase anywhere - COGS% rises mechanically if price is cut, and that is arithmetic, not a sourcing problem. If the seller cannot move cost, the fallback is a price move to Rs 799 (COGS 47.31%, max survivable S/GMV 26.4%), but that must NOT be taken until the launch campaign has its own order data, because the account has no conversion history yet and there is no headroom for a conversion experiment on a cold account.

Watch the age split in the first-week read and narrow to men as a targeting change once there is data. RTO tripwire is set at 55% rather than the 45.70% category benchmark because the seller's own two lifetime orders are both COD and both still sitting in post-purchase hold with zero delivered and zero attempted (get_logistics_partner_data, get_fad_by_segment), and both read 100% RTO on sr delhivery surface at Rs.129 forward logistics per order against a Rs.80.88/AWB benchmark - the account's real RTO exposure may exceed the benchmark, so the tripwire is deliberately set at the worse reading., Ask seller to republish hidden catalogue products and approve a coupon ladder. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask seller whether the stocked but hidden catalogue products should be republished on the storefront (about 30 products are active with 30-60 units in stock each but are not visible), and ask seller to approve a coupon ladder against the account AOV of Rs.2,099 - bands near Rs.4,199 and Rs.6,299 - to be set up once the cost conversation has landed. Reasoning: The catalogue gap is real: get_seller_catalogue returns 8 live visible in-stock products and get_seller_catalogue_quality_summary confirms live_products 8, while get_inventory_check shows roughly 30 further products with is_active=True and stock of 30-60 units each that do not appear in the catalogue read, meaning they are not visible or are flagged OOS. Their per-product is_visible and is_oos flags were NOT CHECKED, so this is a question for the seller rather than an assumption about which are launchable. The coupon gap is measured: get_seller_website_checkout_config returns active_generic_coupon_count 0 and active_generic_coupons empty against aov_for_coupon_check of Rs.2,099, so a healthy ladder wants bands near Rs.4,199 and Rs.6,299. Both are deliberately deferred rather than actioned, because the COGS gap is upstream of both - a discount coupon against a 55% COGS product spends the thinnest part of the margin stack, and at a 25% price cut contribution per order would already be down to Rs.144-168. No catalogue, price, coupon or budget change is being made now, so this action carries no side effect on the running campaign., Confirm the 2 lifetime orders have shipped before scaling spend. |DETAILS| Instruction: Confirm the seller's two existing orders have shipped and left post-purchase hold, and that delivery is being attempted, before any spend above Rs.1,000/day on the launch campaign. Reasoning: Added because the seller's own order history is a risk the strategy report did not surface. get_logistics_partner_data shows both lifetime orders (2 total, 100% of orders) sitting in post-purchase hold with awb_nc 2, delivered 0, in_transit 0, pph 2, on courier 'sr delhivery surface' with zero first-attempt delivery. get_fad_by_segment confirms attempted 0, first_attempt_delivered 0, not_yet_attempted 0 for the window 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-28. get_logistics_partner_payment_mode_data shows both orders on COD with rto_prec 100 and logistics_forward_spend Rs.129 per order against a Rs.80.88/AWB category benchmark. The storefront promises a 6-day delivery (display_delivery_date_non_customised_max_day 6), so an order sitting in PPH is already outside the promise shown to buyers. This is a check, not a diagnosis: the orders are recent and the 2-order sample is far below the 10 non-cancelled orders needed to read an RTO rate in either direction, so the correct response is to verify dispatch works before scaling, not to call an RTO problem. The launch itself is not blocked - Rs.1,000/day is the account's whole envelope and the campaign's job is to buy learning - but no spend above that should go in while dispatch is unproven, because COD orders from a seller whose shipments are stuck would convert learning spend into RTO and return shipping., Hold launch-set prices at Rs.1,999 / Rs.2,199 - no price change. |DETAILS| Instruction: Do not change the selling price on HD001 (Rs.1,999), HD002 (Rs.1,999), HD003 (Rs.2,199), HD004 (Rs.2,199) or HD007 (Rs.2,199). The five product short ids, prices, costs, sizes and links are copied from get_seller_catalogue and get_product_details_by_product_id., Ask seller to confirm metre options and dispatch speed before the campaign goes live. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to confirm in writing what each metre option 2M, 3M, 4M, 5M, 6M and 'Pack Of 2 | 1M' actually includes on the five launch fabrics (PC0111, PC0122, PC0103, PC0058, PC0204) - especially what 'Pack Of 2 | 1M' contains - and to confirm the real dispatch speed behind the 'delivery up to 6 days' promise and the 'NEXT_DAY_DISPATCH' trust badge. Launch Open Audience video campaign at Rs 1,000/day on five sarees. |DETAILS| Instruction: Start one new Meta Open Audience video campaign at Rs. 1,000/day on ad account 28742823632006361, women India-wide excluding Assam, Gujarat, Bihar, West Bengal, Jammu and Kashmir, Tripura and Jharkhand, with five ads (one per saree) at Rs. 200/day each Reasoning: The account has never spent a rupee on marketing (get_seller_account_age: has NEVER recorded marketing spend) and has no campaigns (get_meta_campaign_settings: no Meta campaigns found), so there is no history to diagnose and nothing to reuse. Category resolves to sarees / womens-clothing (get_seller_primary_l2_benchmarks); benchmarks: CTR 3.88%, C2PR 1.08%, CPM Rs 92.72, S/GMV 17.49%, RTO 33.55%, cancellation 17.35% (get_seller_category_level_benchmarking, womens-clothing). The audience shape is carried from three independent comparable saree sellers rather than guessed: -pBo34hw (adset S/GMV 12.69%), dqSU1Z3k, and NXkgAJa1 (11,482 adset orders, 16.27%) — all women-only, age 24-65, India-wide, all at the Rs 999 price point. get_campaign_routing_recommendation returned no route for this seller (NOT CHECKED), so the type is chosen from that audience evidence: Open Audience, because a pre-live account has no customer file to seed a lookalike and the pixel has recorded nothing. DEVIATION from the work order, forced by a Meta constraint: the spec asked for women 24-65, but a new campaign may carry only one narrowing — age OR gender, not both. Gender is kept (women) because all three comparables ran women-only and the whole catalogue is sarees; age is left on Meta's default 18-65 and is the next dial to turn after the first week. No roas_floor is set and no bid cap is set, so the campaign runs LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP — a floor the pixel cannot clear reads as a dead launch. Preconditions verified in this run: ad account 28742823632006361 exists (get_seller_config_build, the seller's only ad account); all five products active, visible, 50 units in stock each (get_inventory_check, one id per call); all geo exclusion keys re-resolved through search_meta_geo_locations — Assam 1725, Gujarat 1729, Bihar 1752, West Bengal 1746 (previously verified) and Jammu and Kashmir 1732, Tripura 1745, Jharkhand 1756 (re-resolved here; all three returned exactly as carried). No cities are excluded, so there is no state-plus-city overlap. Funding: the account's total daily spend goes from Rs 0 to Rs 1,000/day, which is the first-campaign ceiling itself; no other campaign exists to fund it from and none is created. The campaign goes live as it is built and commits its budget from the first day. Five video creatives were generated for this run, one per product, each with its own handle, so no product's ad is blocked on another's render., Ask seller to confirm launch AOV band, then set a 2x/3x coupon ladder. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to confirm the launch AOV band once the first orders land, then set a generic bumper coupon at about 2x that AOV and a generic retention coupon at about 3x that AOV — do not set the bands before the first complete week Reasoning: get_seller_website_checkout_config confirms active_generic_coupon_count is 0 and aov_for_coupon_check is null — the account has no coupon ladder and, being pre-live with zero orders, no AOV to size one against. The launch set sits at Rs 949-Rs 1,299, so the standard 2x/3x AOV ladder is the right shape, but the band must wait for the first real orders: with no prior complete week and a null AOV, any band would be invented. The bands are therefore not set now; this is a seller conversation to be closed once the first week of orders establishes an AOV, and the coupon creation itself is a later action once the seller confirms the band., Raise Maroon Silk Saree (705 KP 5000-Maroon) from Rs. 899 to Rs. 949. |DETAILS| Instruction: Update selling price for SKU 705 KP 5000-Maroon (Maroon Silk Saree For Women) from Rs. 899 to Rs. 949 Reasoning: Current price Rs 899 with cost Rs 299 (get_seller_catalogue and get_inventory_check, both confirmed in this run: selling_price 899, cost_price 299, stock 50, active) — the cheapest item in the launch set and the thinnest margin against Rs 86.17/AWB logistics and 33.55% category RTO (get_seller_category_level_benchmarking, womens-clothing). Rs 899 is the floor of the proven marketplace band, where the leading soft-lichi seller prices Rs 899-999 with roughly 2,000 ratings (https://www.amazon.in/SGF11-Womens-Kanjivaram-Lichi-Blouse/dp/B0C8SYJBYM, https://www.amazon.in/soft-lichi-silk-sarees-for-women/s?k=soft+lichi+silk+sarees+for+women). At Rs 899 the SKU affords a maximum S/GMV of 20.6% (+3.1pp headroom against the 17.49% benchmark); at Rs 949 it affords 22.4% (+4.9pp). The move is 5.6%, inside the 25% cap, and Rs 949 ends in 49. No COGS action is taken: COGS% is 33.3% against a 46.78% category norm, so this is headroom rather than a sourcing problem, and no matched identical product sells at a lower cost (get_internal_pricing_similarity returns no internal match for this catalogue). The other four launch products are deliberately left alone — kONiUhFVHFJV (Rs 999) and IXQHlJ0op5nV (Rs 999) hold, because cutting them to Rs 899 would raise COGS% from 37.0% to 41.2% and drop their maximum affordable S/GMV from 18.2% to 14.1%, below the 17.49% benchmark, a margin mistake dressed as a discount; gK1EspedDvKm (Rs 1,099) and OOzjwuS86mKR (Rs 1,299) already carry +5.9pp and +6.0pp of breakeven headroom. The ~654 catalogue products at Rs 1,299-Rs 1,999 are not in the launch set and are not priced in this plan. One honest note for the operator: the strategy's headroom figures rest on an assumed 12% pre-tax Shopdeck commission, because the seller has no orders and therefore no realised commission rate; re-deriving the stack with RTO and cancellation modelled as revenue leakage gives a tighter ceiling than the strategy's, which is a reason to read this as a genuine test rather than a formality. The seller's own break-even S/GMV is undefined (get_seller_breakeven_sgmv returns empty) because there are no orders, so every figure here is against the 17.49% category benchmark. Note the seller instruction set was NOT CHECKED for this run — an unlooked-up standing instruction on pricing would bind here, so confirm with the seller before applying. This change should land with the campaign, since the Maroon ad headline quotes Rs.949., Ask seller to decide the blouse piece on all five launch sarees. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller to decide before the ads land: either add an unstitched blouse piece to all five launch sarees, or state clearly on each product page and in the ad that the blouse piece is NOT included Reasoning: All five launch products state the saree fabric only, "blouse piece not included unless specified" — confirmed in this run by reading every description (get_product_details_by_product_id for kONiUhFVHFJV, IXQHlJ0op5nV, 3GWQjk7FBR7u, gK1EspedDvKm, OOzjwuS86mKR; each returns the identical note, and each is a 5.5 metre single-SKU saree). On a saree account that is the most likely source of both customer cancellation and RTO, because the buyer sees a saree image on the ad and expects a complete garment at checkout. The one validated comparable in this exact fabric family (-pBo34hw, "Soft Banarasi Lichi Silk Saree with Unstitched Blouse Piece", adset S/GMV 12.69%) includes one. This is a seller pricing/packaging decision, not an operator action, so it carries no action_type and is done by hand. It must land before spend starts, because changing five product pages while Rs 1,000/day is running costs more than settling it first. Note the seller instruction set was NOT CHECKED for this run — an unlooked-up standing instruction on packaging would bind here, so this asks rather than assumes., Add Bestseller Infinite Product Widget to the five launch product pages. |DETAILS| Instruction: Ask the seller for agreement, then add the Bestseller Infinite Product Widget (hygiene details U3gKbP58y6) to the five launch saree product pages: kONiUhFVHFJV, IXQHlJ0op5nV, 3GWQjk7FBR7u, gK1EspedDvKm and OOzjwuS86mKR Reasoning: fetch_hygiene_actions for account_stage hit returns the item "Add Bestseller Infinite Product Widget", details U3gKbP58y6, action_type website_automation, impact medium, seller_consent true — confirmed again in this run. The five products about to carry Rs 1,000/day of traffic are exactly the pages where product discovery matters. The item is marked seller_consent true, so it cannot proceed without the seller, hence it is raised as a seller ask. The second hygiene item, the Product Testimonial Widget (fewer than 10 present, impact low, seller_consent false), is deliberately not given a launch slot: no product has a rating yet because the account has no orders (get_seller_catalogue_quality_summary shows product_quality_lifetime and product_quality_last_15_days both empty), so there is nothing to testimonial. widget_page_id and widget_ids are storefront ids that no tool in this set returns, so they are left unset and the recommendation ships for a growth lead to do by hand — the ids are not constructed from page or widget names.

Enable online payment on the storefront (Razorpay). |DETAILS| Instruction: Three coordinated edits on get_seller_website_checkout_config: (a) integrate Razorpay (preferred — UPI, cards, netbanking, wallets) so is_razorpay=true, (b) add "online" to settings_payment_mode so the list reads "cod, online" (or "online, cod"), and (c) set push_for_online_payments=true. Then run a ₹1 test transaction end-to-end to confirm the gateway is live. Do NOT mark complete until the seller has confirmed in writing that the test transaction cleared and the Razorpay dashboard shows a settled payment. COD must remain enabled and functional throughout — the tripwire is "does enabling online payment break the COD path", and the launch is conditional on COD still working for buyers who choose it. This action MUST land before any paid Meta campaign begins; without it the storefront is COD-only and 25–35% settled RTO is the realistic floor, which makes any ad spend unprofitable from day 1. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) confirms settings_payment_mode="cod", is_razorpay=is_paytm=is_easebuzz=false, push_for_online_payments=false. Hygiene sweep flagged this as HIGH. The launch thesis (a paid Meta campaign on this catalogue) is unworkable on a COD-only storefront because the assortment (apparel, jewellery, accessories) sits in a high-COD, high-RTO category, and the literature on this platform says COD-only stores have a 25–35% settled RTO floor. The tripwire is "did enabling online payment break COD" — online payment has to be added, not replace COD, and the gateway has to be integration-tested, not just toggled., Resolve the expired / null custom domain. |DETAILS| Instruction: Two paths. (a) If the seller has a custom domain: renew it at the registrar, point it at the Shopdeck storefront, and confirm the SSL certificate is valid. (b) If the seller does not have a custom domain: confirm in writing that the default Shopdeck storefront URL is the live storefront and the "expired" flag on custom_domain is a stale signal rather than a real outage. Do NOT mark complete until (a) the storefront URL responds with HTTP 200, and (b) if a custom domain is in use, the SSL certificate validates. This action must land before any paid Meta campaign begins — paid traffic landing on a 404 / failed-SSL storefront burns budget with zero conversion. The seller should set a calendar reminder at day 25 from completion to re-verify the domain is not approaching expiry again. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) shows custom_domain=null. The hygiene sweep flagged this as MED, the strategy stage escalated it to a launch-blocker because paid Meta traffic on a 404 storefront is a 100% budget loss with zero chance of recovery. The verification step (HTTP 200 + valid SSL) is in the instruction, not the metric, because it is a one-time check, not a continuously-watched number. The day-25 reminder belongs in the operator's calendar, not in the action., Set up the first coupon ladder (2 bands at 2x-AOV and 3x-AOV). |DETAILS| Instruction: Create two generic coupons. (1) 2x-AOV band: coupon_code="WELCOME2X", coupon_title="Welcome 2x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=1500, coupon_max_discount_amount=200, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. (2) 3x-AOV band: coupon_code="WELCOME3X", coupon_title="Welcome 3x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=2400, coupon_max_discount_amount=400, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. aov_for_coupon_check is null (no order history), so the bands use the strategy stage's catalogue-derived estimate: AOV ~₹600–800 across the 7 hero SKUs post-reprice, so 2x ≈ ₹1,500 and 3x ≈ ₹2,400. Confirm bands and discount levels with the seller before publishing — keep discounts at 5–10%, not 15%+, so the coupon does not eat margin. The two coupons together count as one ladder; do NOT exceed 2 active generic coupons at this stage. This action is non-blocking for the launch campaign (the launch can run without coupons), but should land before paid traffic begins so a first-time buyer has a lever to convert. The payload below carries band 1 (WELCOME2X); band 2 (WELCOME3X) is the separate action that follows. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) shows active_generic_coupon_count=0, active_generic_coupons=null, aov_for_coupon_check=null. Hygiene sweep and strategy stage both flagged this. With no order history, AOV is unmeasurable, so the bands use the catalogue-derived estimate (₹600–800 across the 7 hero SKUs post-reprice): 2x = ₹1,500, 3x = ₹2,400. The 5–10% discount cap is a margin protection — Shopdeck sellers who run 15%+ coupon discounts on pre-launch products typically see coupon conversion eat the entire marketing margin. The expiry date is 6 months out (2027-04-14) so the coupons do not have to be touched again in this run., Set up the 3x-AOV coupon band. |DETAILS| Instruction: Create the second generic coupon. coupon_code="WELCOME3X", coupon_title="Welcome 3x", coupon_discount_type=percentage, coupon_value=5–10, coupon_min_order_value=2400, coupon_max_discount_amount=400, coupon_expiry_date=2027-04-14. Pair with the 2x band (WELCOME2X) created in the prior action. Confirm the band and discount level with the seller before publishing. Reasoning: Same logic as the 2x band: catalogue-derived AOV estimate ₹600–800, 3x = ₹2,400. The pair together form the 2-band ladder the strategy stage required. Issued as a separate action rather than merged with the 2x band so each band can be confirmed and verified independently — a failed create on the 3x band should not roll back a confirmed 2x band., Install and verify the Meta pixel on the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: Three steps. (1) Install the Meta pixel on the storefront (via the Shopdeck pixel/marketing-settings integration — not a manual code edit). (2) Verify in Events Manager that the pixel fires on the four key events: ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase. Use a test purchase to confirm the Purchase event lands with the right conversion value. (3) Confirm only ONE pixel id is installed (the catalogue-quality summary reported products_with_multiple_pixel_ids=0, so the starting state is clean — keep it that way). This action MUST land before any paid Meta campaign begins: the lookalike seed for week 4+ is built from the pixel's purchase events, and without the pixel the campaign runs on broad-interest targeting with no purchase signal to optimise against for the entire first 30 days. The tripwire is "pixel double-fires" — verify the Events Manager event volume matches the actual test purchase count. Reasoning: Catalogue-quality summary shows products_with_multiple_pixel_ids=0 (clean starting state) and the diagnosis established that the account has zero pixel events on record. Hygiene sweep did not flag a pixel issue (because there is no pixel to flag), but the diagnosis correctly identified that without a verified pixel the launch campaign has no signal. The strategy stage escalated this to a launch-blocker in item 6 of the work order. The instruction explicitly names all four events and a test-purchase verification, because the most common failure mode is installing a pixel that fires on PageView but not on Purchase., Add Facebook and Instagram social links to the storefront. |DETAILS| Instruction: In the storefront settings, set facebook_url to the seller's active Facebook page URL and instagram_url to the seller's active Instagram profile URL. Confirm both URLs are correct and point at pages the seller actively controls — not placeholder accounts, not personal profiles, and not the wrong brand. Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) shows facebook_url=null and instagram_url=null. This action is non-blocking — it can run in parallel with the launch-blocker gate and does not have to land before the launch campaign begins. The tripwire is "URL is a placeholder account" — confirm the seller controls both pages and that the pages are about this store's brand, not a different one. Reasoning: Live config (re-verified 2026-10-14) shows facebook_url=null, instagram_url=null. Hygiene sweep flagged this as MED, strategy stage confirmed. The action is non-blocking (the launch can run without social links) but the strategy stage placed it in the launch-blocker bundle as a small parallel fix. The placeholder-account tripwire is the commonest failure here — a seller copy-pastes the wrong URL or a test page they set up months ago., Bulk-clean the 47,083 placeholder SKUs from the catalogue. |DETAILS| Instruction: PREFERRED PATH — bulk-soft-delete the placeholder SKUs in the catalogue admin. The placeholder cohort occupies ~47,083 of the 47,100 live products and shares the SKU prefix family prdductti*, prductti*, prdumil*, prduoomil*, pruoomil* with prices ₹350/₹549 and cost ₹270. Real products (the 17 in the catalogue tail, with MP* seller_sku_ids, hand-named titles, real category tags and distinct prices) MUST be preserved. BEFORE the bulk delete, take a backup of the 17 real product short_ids so an accidental delete is recoverable: mgP13ugi, Qk4jaYWA, Sk2awLUS, 9fjacPG2, EkiFC66Z, hVyUvamU, -smoLbl_, va9bv7E_, 2H6-d9bZ, e6-Vp0yZ, rDZ1jIMV, MaYbnMmD plus the remaining 5 home / book / decor products the operator can confirm via get_seller_catalogue. FALLBACK PATH — if Shopdeck operations cannot do a bulk delete, leave the placeholders visible but apply the SKU-prefix exclusion set as a product-set filter on every Meta campaign that pulls from the catalogue. The hygiene findings on the 1,051 OOS SKUs, the ~20,730 under-50% MRP SKUs and the 28,158 under-2-image SKUs almost all sit inside the placeholder cohort and collapse to this same fix. Watch live_catalogue_count drop from ~47,100 to ~17–25, and confirm the 1,051 OOS finding drops to near zero. Reasoning: The diagnosis and strategy stage both established that 47,083 of 47,100 live products are placeholder SKUs identifiable by SKU prefix (prdductti*, prductti*, prdumil*, prduoomil*, pruoomil*), price grid (₹350/₹549), and cost (₹270). The catalogue-quality summary independently confirmed: out_of_stock_products=1,051, products_discounted_under_50pct=20,730 (100% prductti*/prdumil* in the sample), products_with_under_2_images=28,158 (100% prdductti*/prductti* in the sample). All three hygiene findings collapse to the placeholder cleanup. Without this fix, any catalogue-driven Meta campaign (Advantage+, DPA) will spend 99.8% on dead listings — the SKU-prefix filter is the documented fallback if Shopdeck operations cannot perform a bulk delete. The 17 real product IDs are spelled out so the operator can build the backup before the delete and so the SKU-prefix exclusion has a clean allowlist., Fill the 7 hero product cards (descriptions + 2+ images). |DETAILS| Instruction: For each of the 7 hero SKUs (mgP13ugi, Qk4jaYWA, Sk2awLUS, 9fjacPG2, EkiFC66Z, hVyUvamU, -smoLbl_), add: (a) a 200+ character product description covering fabric, fit, occasion, care, sizing, and what is included in the pack; (b) 2+ product images per SKU (run get_product_images against each short_id to confirm current image counts and fill gaps). All 7 currently have description="" (re-verified 2026-10-14). Prioritise the 5 launch heroes: saree (mgP13ugi), bangles (Qk4jaYWA), yoga pants (Sk2awLUS), tee (-smoLbl_), and bra (hVyUvamU). Re-read each description against the catalogue title before publishing to catch wrong-copy mistakes. This action can run in parallel with the launch-blocker gate (items 1, 2, 3, 6) — the launch campaign will underperform if these cards are still empty when ads go live, but the campaign will not break. The catalogue-quality summary reported products_with_under_2_images=28,158 (100% placeholder cohort in the sample), so the count of "real products needing images" is expected to drop to 0 once the placeholder cleanup in item 3 lands. Reasoning: get_product_details_by_product_id re-verified 2026-10-14 confirms description="" on all 7 hero SKUs. The diagnosis and strategy stage both flagged this. Empty descriptions drop Meta's relevance score and on-site conversion; the 200-character floor is a meaningful minimum (the median catalogue description is ~660 chars, so 200+ is achievable without padding). The 2+ image floor is the same: catalogue-quality said 28,158 products are under 2 images, but those are 100% placeholder cohort in the sample, so the real-product count is 0 after the placeholder cleanup. The instruction calls this out so the operator does not interpret 28,158 as a 7-card fix., Replace the 4 outdated Amazon-ASIN testimonials. |DETAILS| Instruction: Remove the 4 Amazon-ASIN testimonials currently tagged on this catalogue: amazon_B0GYZYGJJS (on product nte2QfbN), amazon_B0H166TLQV (on MMo5R7gl), amazon_B0GRWW5RZN (on VjD3gpmp), amazon_B0GRN126GN (on etm-NSZ7) — re-verified 2026-10-14 from get_seller_testimonial_coverage, all four are flagged as "testimonial_older_than_2_months". Amazon ASINs on a Shopdeck storefront are a mismatch — they break buyer trust and have no provenance to the seller's own products. If the seller has real testimonials (from delivered orders) for the 17 real products, tag those products with the seller's own testimonials. If not, the seller can skip the second step until first orders come in. This action is non-blocking — it can run in parallel with the launch-blocker gate. Tripwire: after replacement, re-check get_seller_testimonial_coverage shows no amazon_* short_ids, and the seller's own testimonials (if any were added) are not themselves older than 2 months. Reasoning: get_seller_testimonial_coverage re-verified 2026-10-14: the four product ids (nte2QfbN, MMo5R7gl, VjD3gpmp, etm-NSZ7) all have testimonials with the amazon_* prefix, all flagged "testimonial_older_than_2_months". Hygiene sweep flagged this as MED, strategy stage confirmed. The action is non-blocking — the launch can run without the testimonial replacement — but Amazon-ASIN testimonials on a non-Amazon storefront are a low-trust signal worth removing. The four product ids and the four ASINs are spelled out so the operator does not have to re-derive them.
